summary.headline: IndiaMART Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore, with EBITDA margin of 37% and paying suppliers down 615 QoQ to 2,17,000.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore and consolidated collections grew 9% to Rs 443 crore, while deferred revenue rose 16% to Rs 2,029 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 159 crore (37% margin) and net profit was Rs 91 crore, with other income negative at Rs 8 crore due to bond-yield MTM losses. Paying suppliers fell by 615 QoQ to 2,17,000, attributed mainly to elevated Silver subscription churn. Management said unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined for about two quarters, which it linked to AI-driven search changes and its own decision to restrict data access, with a 10-15% loss from peak levels.

financial_highlights.change: Due to MTM losses from bond yield increase; management calls it notional

segments.name: IndiaMART marketplace
segments.commentary: Collections Rs 394 crore (+8% YoY) standalone; 27 million unique business enquiries in Q2; paying suppliers 2,17,000 after net decline of 615 in the quarter. Gold and Platinum are about 50% of customers and about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: BUSY Infotech
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations Rs 37 crore (+27% YoY), billing Rs 46 crore (+20% YoY), deferred revenue about Rs 155 crore (+40% YoY), cash from operations about Rs 12 crore. About 11,000 new licences sold in Q2, taking the total to 4,66,000.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 33% reiterated; management called it conservative, and Q2 margin was 37% on a consolidated basis.

Management said margins are not comparable quarter to quarter because costs are upfront and revenue recognised over up to 18 months; it plans to invest more heavily in sales once Silver churn is better understood.
Management expects value and volume growth to be balanced over the next 2-3 years, versus historically about 10% value and 10% volume growth.
BUSY said comparable growth from Q3 onwards should be in line with the 20-30% overall growth rate it has been seeing.
No guidance on when Silver churn will improve; management has stopped giving that guidance.
capex_capacity: Management said 100% of expenses, including manpower and AI research, are expensed; no subsidiary capitalises manpower or software costs.
Advertising spend running at Rs 8-9 crore per quarter, nearing a Rs 10 crore per quarter budget, focused on the top quartile of categories.
Pilots underway for credit facilitation (IndiaMART Finance) and a paid verified business buyer programme; no significant capital committed yet.
Next ESOP pool decision to be taken by the board at financial year end; last pools were in 2018, 2022 and 2025.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined YoY for about two quarters; management attributes 10-15% loss from best-ever highs to Google AI Overviews and to restricting proprietary data behind logins.
Management said ARPU growth has historically run 5-10% and revenue growth is now 8-10%; growth has come mostly from value (ARPU and upsell) rather than volume over the last two to three years.
Silver 12-month retention is about 10% lower than four to five years ago, which management cites as the main gap to 10% volume and 10% value growth.
Around 10% of buyer traffic now comes through paid advertising, with 20-40% cannibalisation of organic traffic depending on the area.
Trust Assurance programme protects buyers up to Rs 5 lakh on purchases from verified bank accounts and TrustSEAL suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Why are active buyers and unique business enquiries declining, and is GenAI search a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: AI Overviews now cover 50% or more of searches, causing a 10-15% decline from peak. It has put more data behind logins and stopped showing some proprietary data to search engines and LLMs, and it accepts losing 10-20% of current enquiries to protect data.

qa_highlights.question: Is IndiaMART moving toward a transaction marketplace, as JustDial reportedly aspires to?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not going fully marketplace or away from listings, but wants to get closer to transactions, citing its earlier Tolexo and payment platform attempts and its current credit facilitation work.

qa_highlights.question: Where is AI showing up in the business, and is it monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 20+ AI use cases and voice AI serving 80,000-100,000 buyers daily, and said benefits are cost, intelligence and time. It said net benefit is volatile over 2-4 years and it does not expect AI to show up directly in enquiries yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost fall, and what is the outlook for personnel cost leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Jitin Diwan said ESOP expense declines each year under the graded design, and the current level is the baseline until the next pool. Management said near-term AI experimentation adds cost and savings are reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the lending and credit facilitation business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to support marketplace transactions for high-value equipment, not to become a lender. Pilots are small and will be reported quarterly; no pre-approved credit lines yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BUSY collection growth, which has appeared to decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Brijesh Agrawal said Q1 and Q2 FY27 growth was inflated by a higher base from a billing methodology change and customer win-back in the prior year; comparable growth should be 20-30% from Q3.

risks_watch: Paying supplier base declined by 615 QoQ; Silver churn has not yet improved and no timeline is given.
Unique enquiries and active buyers are down 10-15% from peak, with AI search and data restrictions cited as the drivers.
Other income is negative (Rs 8 crore) from bond MTM losses; management expects reversal over the next few quarters.
Credit facilitation and buyer monetisation programmes are at pilot stage with undefined capital and first-loss exposure.
Margin of 37% in Q2 reflects low sales investment; management plans to step up sales spend, which could compress margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, the balance sheet and AI deployment, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Silver churn, buyer volume trends, timing of recovery and credit business economics, repeatedly saying outcomes are unknown and that it will report when results are material.
key_quotes: So yes, 10%, 15% decline on that is happening.
We are very certain, and we are not experimenting.
Nobody can predict next two, three quarters or next two, three years.
100% of our expense are expensed out, whether it is in the manpower, whether it is in the AI research or anywhere else.

growth.why: No capacity additions; management expects revenue growth of 8-10% driven mainly by ARPU/value, with value and volume balanced over 2-3 years, but enquiries and active buyers have declined for about two quarters and Silver churn has no timeline for improvement.
